hero.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up summer traffic enforcement after speeding complaints
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro said he cares about his family and everyone else's loved ones who drive on these roadways and wants to make the community safer. He is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and is also placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding and most recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues described stopping a girl doing 72 mph on Midway Road and clocking someone at 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues said his top speed recorded was 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

Local residents say the problem is hard to miss. Ashley, a St. Lucie County resident, said the situation is insane and nobody slows down. Jessica, another local driver, echoed those concerns and said drivers are just careless and cut people off. The combination of increased enforcement and community complaints underscores the severity of speeding issues across St. Lucie County roadways this summer.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out during construction.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on, she said.

The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: JetBlue cuts direct flights from Vero Beach to New York JFK in September
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport on Sept. 9, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The airline said in a statement to WPTV that demand for the new route has not materialized as hoped. The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a "game changer" for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The airport hoped the JFK connection would attract more passengers and increase tourism to the region, but those expectations did not translate into sufficient demand to sustain the route.

JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline will provide full refunds to all customers affected by the route cancellation.

cards.headline: Donalds leads Florida GOP primary as Jolly consolidates Democratic support ahead of August vote
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly have emerged as frontrunners in Florida's gubernatorial primary race with the August 18 primary approaching. Donalds holds a commanding advantage in Republican polling and fundraising, while Jolly has consolidated support in the Democratic contest as opponents scramble for a late breakthrough in the closing weeks.

A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48%, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8%, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has announced more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation and holds President Donald Trump's endorsement. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins as lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary. During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds despite his deficit in polling and fundraising, saying the race is between him and Donalds with a clear path forward. Collins also urged Renner to leave the race and argued Donalds could struggle in a general election.

Fishback faces pressure on two fronts. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign. Collins is also challenging Fishback's candidacy in court, alleging he lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots.

Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni, who federal prosecutors allege stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit managing trust funds for people with disabilities. Govoni and accountant John Witeck have been charged with operating the scheme from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress, and Govoni served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft. A June Change Research survey commissioned by Freedom Project USA showed Jolly leading Donalds 47% to 42% among registered voters, though respondents were shown prepared descriptions of both candidates before being asked whom they supported.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low passenger demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue told WPTV that demand for the new route has not materialized as hoped. The airline will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. Despite the initial optimism surrounding the route's debut, passenger numbers failed to meet the airline's expectations over the following months.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The loss of the JFK route represents a setback for the airport's efforts to grow its connectivity options, though travelers will still have access to the Northeast through the remaining Boston service. The airport had hoped the JFK route would attract both tourists visiting the Treasure Coast and residents seeking convenient access to New York.

JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline's decision highlights the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining new commercial routes, even when they initially generate excitement among local communities and travelers.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents return to St. Lucie County condos after two years
cards.teaser: Residents of Villa Del Sol in St. Lucie County are returning home after nearly two years of displacement following structural damage that forced their evacuation.
cards.body:
Residents of Villa Del Sol in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos. Residents said they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return and obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson was the first to share with WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. She described the work still underway at the property, saying they are still moving the dirt back under the buildings. Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot.

Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia. Eric said the financial toll has been severe and he pretty much had to drain out all his savings accounts and all his 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors like Eric Johnson who cannot return.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts finish top 15 nationally, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month, qualifying for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine each found their way to gymnastics through different paths but now compete as one unit on the national stage. Rose-Daris was drawn to the sport because she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was inspired by watching gymnasts on YouTube and seeing how amazing and fun it looked. Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things.

Head Coach Candice Lazuka described the season as strong, with the team competing locally and traveling before advancing to states and regionals. The progression through different competition levels set the stage for their appearance at the national championships. At AAU Nationals in Knoxville last month, the gymnasts came close to a perfect score, earning a 9.9. Lazuka noted that achieving a perfect 10 is difficult, making their near-perfect performance particularly impressive.

The top 15 finish at nationals earned the team qualification for the Junior Olympics scheduled for next month in Iowa. Rose-Daris expressed excitement about the upcoming competition, saying it will be really fun to go to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings about the qualification as happy and exciting at the same time. The opportunity to compete at the Junior Olympics represents a major milestone for the young gymnasts.

Looking ahead to the competition in Iowa, Rine has set a specific goal for herself. She said her focus heading into the Junior Olympics is getting first place on floors. The team's advancement to this elite level of competition represents a significant achievement for the local gymnastics program. The three gymnasts who started in the sport for different reasons have now reached one of the highest levels of youth competition together, demonstrating how their individual journeys have merged into collective success on the national stage.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 with late goals to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored twice in the final minutes Wednesday to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinal, with Enzo Fernandez equalizing in the 85th minute and Lautaro Martinez heading in the winner in stoppage time.
cards.body:
Argentina scored twice in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 in a World Cup semifinal on Wednesday, keeping the defending champions alive for back-to-back titles. Trailing 1-0 after Anthony Gordon scored for England in the 55th minute, Argentina equalized when Enzo Fernandez swept in a shot from outside the box in the 85th minute after receiving a pass from Lionel Messi. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for substitute Lautaro Martinez to head in the winning goal. Martinez said he told teammate Alexis Mac Allister before the match that he was going to come on and win it. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves and Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina mounted wave after wave of attacks.

The loss marks the third time England has fallen short in World Cup semifinals, following defeats to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, staff and fans after working so hard to reach this stage. Argentina will face Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni praised the collectiveness and brotherhood of his team, saying they were ready to go home knowing they had left everything on the pitch. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk and rhythm, which freed them up while England played with the feeling they had a lot to lose.

cards.headline: World Cup semifinals set with England, Argentina, Spain and France advancing
cards.teaser: England and Argentina advanced through quarterfinal victories over the weekend to complete the World Cup semifinal lineup alongside Spain and France, with all four highest-ranked teams reaching the final four.
cards.body:
England advanced to the World Cup semifinals after defeating Norway with two goals from Jude Bellingham, while Argentina needed extra time to beat Switzerland and reach the last four, with Julián Alvarez scoring in extra time to help his team through. The four highest-ranked teams in the world have reached the semifinals, though none took a straightforward path to get there. Argentina has scored the most goals of any team in the competition with 17 and has the added experience of many squad members who won the title in 2022.

England has relied heavily on Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham, who have each scored six goals in the tournament. Both players have produced match-winning moments even as the team has looked disjointed and vulnerable defensively. England last reached a World Cup semifinal in 2018, losing to Croatia on that occasion. Spain and France round out the semifinal matchups, with France considered by many to be the tournament favorite despite barely getting out of first gear. Spain recently beat France in the semifinals of Euro 2024, a tournament it won, and also defeated France in the Nations League last year. Spain has conceded just one goal the entire tournament.

hero.headline: Delray Beach dance studio hosts Bridgerton-themed masquerade gala July 24 for ninth anniversary
hero.teaser: Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach is celebrating nine years with a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala featuring themed décor and ballroom dancing.
hero.body:
Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, located at 247 SE Sixth Ave., is hosting a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala on July 24 to celebrate its ninth anniversary. The studio is owned by world champion dancers Mar Martinez and Clifton Sepulveda. According to the studio, the event will feature themed décor, dancing and a celebration of the studio's growth over the past nine years. The studio has built a reputation for welcoming dancers of all experience levels, from beginners to competitive performers.

The studio is launching a Summer Boot Camp series beginning July 18 and continuing every Saturday through August. According to Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, the classes are designed to help participants learn ballroom and Latin dance fundamentals in a fun, supportive environment. Another upcoming event is a DJ Latin Dance Night open to the public on July 31 from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Martinez and Sepulveda are also preparing to teach a dance class at Florida Atlantic University beginning in August. More information about upcoming events and classes is available at FredAstaireDelrayBeach.com.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, announces new koala joey named Bonza
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo has extended its Kids Free promotion and revealed its newest koala joey is a male named Bonza, Aussie slang for awesome.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Zoo extended its Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, allowing up to four children ages 3 to 12 to receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, said the extension helps local families enjoy affordable outings during summer while supporting the zoo's conservation mission.

The zoo announced its newest koala joey is officially a boy and has been named Bonza, which is Aussie slang for awesome or excellent. Zoo staff members from departments ranging from accounting to marketing helped document and share the koala family's journey with the public.

Palm Beach Zoo is also bringing back its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. Themed nights include Paws & Santa Claus in July, Tails & Touchdowns in August, and Decades After Dark in September, featuring live entertainment from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance cuts Florida homeowners rates by 5.6%, introduces disappearing deductible
cards.teaser: The Ormond Beach-based insurer is the latest Florida company to reduce rates, citing fewer lawsuits from state reforms.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said all those savings the company is required to pass along to customers, and they have been.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year a customer's deductible goes down 20 percent as long as they don't have a loss. Once a customer has a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Premiums in South Florida generally run high, and online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

hero.headline: Palm City weather spotter with Navy meteorology background discusses forecasting technology evolution
hero.teaser: Brian Botley, a Palm City resident and WPTV Weather Spotter, shared how his Navy training in meteorology led to a lifelong passion for tracking weather in the Treasure Coast.
hero.body:
Brian Botley, a Palm City WPTV Weather Spotter, spoke with WPTV First Alert Weather Meteorologist James Wieland about how weather forecasting has evolved over the decades. Botley's interest in weather began when he moved to Oakland Park in 1951, where his father was always plotting hurricanes. He went into the Navy and was picked to attend Aerographer's Mate School in Lakehurst.

Botley's first job was plotting weather maps. Satellites started appearing around 1961 or 1962, but the coverage was nothing like what exists now. Wieland showed Botley the technology used in today's weather coverage and walked him through how computer models and modern radar systems have transformed forecasting. Botley said joining WPTV's Weather Spotter program felt like a natural extension of something he was already doing on his own, explaining that he does weather tracking all the time and thought it might be fun because there are other people involved in the program.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

The airline will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. Despite the initial optimism surrounding the route's debut, passenger numbers failed to meet the airline's expectations over the following months.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The loss of the JFK route represents a setback for the airport's efforts to grow its connectivity options, though travelers will still have access to the Northeast through the remaining Boston service. The airport had hoped the JFK route would attract both tourists visiting the Treasure Coast and residents seeking convenient access to New York.

JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline's decision highlights the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining new commercial routes, even when they initially generate excitement among local communities and travelers.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK flights after nine months of service
cards.teaser: Low passenger demand has forced JetBlue to cancel its direct route between Vero Beach and New York's JFK Airport.
cards.body:
JetBlue is discontinuing service between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport on Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began. The airline cited insufficient passenger demand for the route that launched in December 2025.

The cancellation presents a challenge for Treasure Coast tourism connectivity and traveler access to one of the nation's major airports. JetBlue will continue operating its Boston route from Vero Beach.
